correctness.finding: PASS. The disk automorphism sends the higher Neil constraint to h=z^(m+1)phi with ||phi||∞<=1. For offsets 0<=k<=m, the inequality 2(m+1)>m+1+k removes every h^2 term from the relevant section, yielding exactly S_{m+1+k}f=a+(1-|a|^2)z^(m+1)S_k phi. Optimizing over |a| gives the sharp threshold r^(m+1)M_k(r)<=1/2. The Szász factorization with b_j=binom(2j,j)/4^j gives M_k(r)=sum b_j^2 r^(k-2j) whenever the associated truncation is zero-free in the disk; Eneström–Kakeya proves the stated general range. The k=2 boundary calculation gives 459/512<1. For k=3, independently carrying the Möbius transform through gives 7s^3+105s^2+21s+83; the cubic Hurwitz inequality is satisfied, yielding the improved 3/4 zero-free threshold. The four displayed polynomial equations and the fixed-k asymptotic constants follow by direct expansion.

originality.finding: PASS, narrowly scoped. Das–Sarkar's September 2026 result concerns the ordinary Neil algebra m=1 and includes the cubic 4r^3+r-2=0. The submitted theorem extends to the higher constraints C+z^(m+1)H∞, supplies a uniform early-section reduction, and derives new exact families and asymptotics. The underlying Szász coefficient theorem, Rogosinski/Fejér machinery, Eneström–Kakeya, and Hurwitz criterion are classical. A 1942 Manning paper on derivatives of sections is title-adjacent, but open-access retrieval failed and authorized institutional retrieval returned no verified PDF; it was therefore not claimed as read. Its accessible metadata did not establish a result covering these higher-Neil radii, so it remains a disclosed residual rather than a decisive blocker.

scientific_value.finding: PASS. The exact reduction converts a family of constrained section-radius problems into finite Schur coefficient functionals and produces explicit sharp radii beyond the m=1 case, including three new early-section families and a clear asymptotic hierarchy. It is a meaningful structural extension of a very recent sharp Neil-algebra theorem, while appropriately stopping before claiming the full simultaneous radius for all sections.
